title: eRASS1 detects X-rays 2.3 times more often in Gaia white-dwarf-candidate astrometric binaries than in matched single stars; the excess is in hot-white-dwarf systems with 0.2-0.5 d TESS periods
abstract: Question: Are the main-sequence stars in Gaia DR3 astrometric binaries with probable white-dwarf (WD) companions (the NCE class of Shahaf et al. 2024) more X-ray active than matched single stars, and why? Method: We compared eROSITA eRASS1 stellar identifications (HamStar v1.1) of 1,592 NCE and 3,488 red-excess (RCE, probable triple) systems in the eRASS1-DE half sky, and of 12,866 astrometric binaries with secure main-sequence companions (ABI), with 10 matched single stars per system. We tested GALEX UV excess, kinematics, Gaia RV ranges against the astrometric orbit, eRASS1 hardness and TESS full-frame-image periods. Results: eRASS1 detects 33 NCE systems against 14.2 expected (ratio 2.3, 95% CI 1.6-3.3), 123 RCE systems against 39.4 (3.1), and 372 ABI systems against 402 (0.92, no excess). For primaries below 0.95 solar masses, 10 of 54 NCE systems with UV excess (hot WD) are X-ray sources, against 6 of 475 without UV excess (p = 3e-7) and 1 of 38 RCE systems with UV excess. Detected NCE systems are kinematically older than detected single stars (median tangential velocity 37 against 22 km/s, p = 5e-4); ABI systems show no difference. The X-ray spectra are coronal, not supersoft. In TESS, 10 of 32 detected NCE systems vary with periods below 1 d (0 of 28 detected RCE systems), with larger amplitudes; all five hot-WD X-ray systems have periods of 0.24-0.54 d. Gaia RVs show a hidden inner binary in one of 15 testable detected NCE systems (Gaia DR3 6416572288572864512, P = 0.3896 d). Interpretation: activity starts when the WD forms. Accretion spin-up of the main-sequence star or hidden post-common-envelope binaries in triples can explain the data. Limitations: half sky; probabilistic X-ray identifications; one TESS sector per star without centroid tests; RV test only for bright stars; no spectra.

display.caption: eRASS1 detection rate of each class divided by the rate of 10 matched single stars per system, with 95% bootstrap intervals. NCE = no red excess (probable WD companion), RCE = red excess (probable triple), ABI = secure main-sequence companion. The NCE excess is concentrated in systems with a GALEX UV excess.
X-ray detected fraction for primaries below 0.95 solar masses, split by the GALEX near-UV class of Shahaf et al. (2024). Dotted lines: matched single stars. Error bars: Wilson 95% intervals.

Significant TESS periods (FAP < 0.001, P < 6 d) against amplitude corrected for the target flux share in the aperture. Circles mark X-ray detected NCE systems with a hot-WD UV colour (FUV-NUV < 0.3); all have periods of 0.24-0.54 d.
